reference: Shaheen et al., Food Composition Table for Bangladesh (2013), values per 100 g edible portion. Weights below are specified test inputs, not observations of served meals.

reference_cases.description: 150 g plain cooked BR-28 rice, no salt or oil
100 g cooked mashed masoor lentils with no extra cooking liquid, oil or salt
50 g edible farmed chicken egg, boiled without salt, shell removed
120 g plain boiled Diamond potatoes, without added salt or fat
100 g edible ripe raw Sagar banana, peel removed
150 g plain boiled BR-28 rice, 100 g boiled masoor lentils with no oil, and a 50 g boiled farmed chicken egg without the shell

illustrative_cases.description: One medium bowl of vegetable khichuri with a little mustard oil.
One restaurant portion of chicken biryani, with one drumstick.
One plate of rice and a medium piece of rui in fish curry.
One scoop of aloo bhorta with mustard oil and onions, and one cup cooked rice.
One bowl of dry chana and a small whole wheat roti.
Six fuchka with potato and chickpea stuffing and tamarind water.
Medium bowl of chotpoti with half a boiled egg.
One small paper cone of jhalmuri.
Two steamed bhapa pitha with coconut and date palm jaggery.
Two canteen parathas with egg bhaji.
Chicken polao, one plate with a medium piece of chicken.
One small bowl of stir-fried red amaranth and one cup rice.
Half a cup of sweet mishti doi.
One small cup of milk tea and two teaspoons of sugar.
